bib.title: MEM1: Learning to Synergize Memory and Reasoning for Efficient Long-Horizon Agents

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only for lineage; everything else read.

question: Can a language agent learn, through end-to-end RL, to consolidate its memory inside its reasoning so that context stays near-constant over long multi-turn tasks without losing accuracy?
hypothesis: Reasoning can double as working memory: if the context is pruned each turn and reward depends on information gathered earlier, the agent will learn to keep only what is essential in a single internal state.
contributions: MEM1, an end-to-end RL framework that keeps constant memory by updating a shared internal state <IS> that merges reasoning and memory consolidation
A masked-trajectory method (2D attention mask) so PPO policy gradients are valid under context pruning
A scalable task-augmentation recipe that composes N single-objective QA questions into multi-objective long-horizon tasks
Experiments on internal-retrieval QA, open-web QA and WebShop showing better or comparable accuracy with lower memory and latency

method.summary: Each turn the agent emits <IS> (reasoning plus consolidated memory) then a <query> or <answer>; after each turn all previous-turn tags are pruned, leaving the question, latest IS, query and info. Trained with PPO from Qwen2.5-7B Base using a masked trajectory so token advantages are computed under the pruned contexts. Trained on 2-objective composite HotpotQA/NQ QA (outcome-only exact-match reward) and separately on WebShop; tested on up to 16-objective QA, single-objective Wiki QA and zero-shot online web QA.
method.task: multi-turn agentic QA with retrieval, and WebShop navigation; RL for memory consolidation

training.objective: PPO with token-level advantages, critic, KL penalty; reward = exact match for QA (outcome only, no format reward or intermediate reward), built-in environment reward for WebShop
training.lr_schedule: linear warmup of 50 steps (decay not stated)
training.batch_size: data batch size 64, mini batch size 64

other.framework: veRL for RL, Swift for SFT
other.max turns: 6 for 1 to 4 objectives, 20 for harder tasks
other.hint: [HINT: YOU HAVE {turns_left} TURNS LEFT] prepended inside <info>
other.attention mask: 2D mask for objective computation plus 1D info mask; position ids not duplicated (App A.7)
other.training steps seen: read from Fig 6: phases to roughly step 250+; total not stated
other.SFT and instruct starts: authors say RL from base beat instruction-tuned and SFT starts

inference.samples: not stated; tables report mean ± error for efficiency metrics, run count not given
inference.prompting: Prompt 1 (multi-objective QA), Prompt 2 (single QA), Prompt 3 (WebShop); XML tags <think>/<search>/<information>/<answer> in prompts, <IS>/<query>/<info> in text
inference.retrieval: Local Wiki: Faiss-GPU with E5 Base, 3 passages per retrieval; Web: Serper API top 10 results

other.serving: vLLM with automatic prefix caching, single H200, 10 concurrent threads

metrics.name: Exact Match (EM)
metrics.definition: Answer extracted between <answer> tags; multi-objective answers separated by semicolons; 0 if tags mismatched or answer count wrong, else 1 point per correct answer
metrics.unit: count per task (max equals number of objectives)

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: Word-level F1 vs ground truth, max over ground truths; multi-objective F1 is the sum over sub-questions

metrics.name: Peak token usage
metrics.definition: Max tokens (GPT-4o-mini tokenizer) in any single sequence in the trajectory, system prompt excluded

metrics.name: Dependency
metrics.definition: sum over steps of (2*n_o + n_p) * n_o / 2, n_p prefix tokens, n_o output tokens, system prompt ignored

metrics.name: Inference time
metrics.definition: Total elapsed time per trajectory on single H200, 10 threads, vLLM

eval.protocol: Test sets from original papers; efficiency metrics reported with ± values (nature of ± not defined); number of runs and seeds not stated; no significance test.

prompts.text: You will answer multiple complex questions using iterative reasoning, summarization, and web search. At each step, you will see the questions, a cumulative summary of relevant information, the current search query, and search results (except in the first step, where only the questions are provided). Your task is to: 1. Perform reasoning and update a cumulative, concise summary within <think> ... </think>. This acts as persistent memory and must include all essential information from previous <think> and <information> tags. 2. Then choose one of the following actions: - If any question remains unanswered, issue a single query for one question inside <search> ... </search>. The query should consist of keywords or a short phrase. Only search one question at a time. - If all questions are answered, provide the final answers—separated by semicolons—within <answer> answer1; answer2; ... </answer>. The answers must be concise, contain only essential words, and avoid any explanations. Important: - Always follow this structure after <information> or the initial questions: <think> ... </think><search> ... </search> or <think> ... </think><answer> ... </answer>. - Do not search multiple queries or questions simultaneously. Answer the following questions:[QUESTIONS]
You are browsing an online shop.

limits: Authors concede MEM1 assumes environments with well-defined, verifiable rewards; open-ended tasks with sparse or noisy reward are future work.
Position ids are not duplicated, so the masked attention does not fully recover the original attention (App A.7); authors claim no significant effect, no ablation shown.
Training steps, seeds, number of eval runs, critic size, KL coefficient, dataset sizes and optimiser are not stated; no significance tests.
EM scale for multi-objective tasks (e.g. 1.97 at 16 objectives) is a per-task count whose normalisation is not defined; results are one 7B base model.
Table 3 and text disagree on 'highest EM' (MEM1-QA 0.405 below Search-R1 0.445 and 14B 0.422).
Baseline collapse at high objective counts caps their peak tokens, so peak-token ratios depend on collapse behaviour (Fig 4 caption).
Peak tokens exclude system prompt and use GPT-4o-mini tokenizer; peak token is a proxy for memory, not measured GPU memory.
MEM1 at 2 objectives is below Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct (0.709 vs 0.732 EM); the A-MEM 16-objective EM (0.730) is higher than the 14B model, though lower than MEM1.

terms.definition: A compact element in which the agent interleaves reasoning and consolidated memory; the only memory retained between turns
Stitched full trajectory with a 2D attention mask restricting each token to the context that was retained when it was generated, so policy-gradient ratios stay valid
Composite query formed by interleaving N questions from a QA corpus, requiring answers to all (semicolon separated)
